quick.summary: Why a test can win and still hurt, and the metric that warns you.
quick.takeaway: Pick one metric that must not get worse.

beats.line: Our test raised sign ups. Then support tickets doubled. What did we miss?
A guardrail. A metric that must not get worse.
Can I just say a do not break metric?
That works too. A metric you promise not to break.
Choose it before the test, next to your main metric.
If the main one wins but the guardrail breaks, it is not a win.
So we check tickets, refunds or speed alongside sign ups?
One or two of those, picked in advance.
Sign ups up, tickets doubled. Not a win yet.
Exactly. Now the team fixes the cost first.

quiz.question: A test raises sign ups but doubles support tickets. How should you read it?
options: Not a clear win, because a guardrail got worse
A clear win, because sign ups rose
A failure, because tickets matter more
Ignore tickets, they are a different team
quiz.explanation: A guardrail metric shows the cost of a change; a win that breaks it needs fixing first.

quiz.question: A guardrail metric is chosen after the test, once you see what moved.
quiz.explanation: It is chosen before the test, alongside the main metric, so the result cannot be bent later.
